page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It provides dedicated CPU allocation with 2 threads per core, 55 MB of L3 cache, and x86_64 instruction extensions including AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2. No local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs are included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark testing demonstrates low overall processor throughput, with a PassMark CPU score of 3564.93 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1973.0. Single-core performance reflects similar baseline compute levels, scoring 897.0 in Geekbench and 1106.18 in stress-ng CPU tests. Conversely, the memory subsystem achieves an average PassMark memory score of 1969.62, though large-block uncached memory read bandwidth caps at 24.7 GB/sec. Small 135M model LLM text generation reaches an average speed of 102.59 tokens/sec, whereas static web serving throughput registers at 2.66 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to vCPU allocation provides economical RAM availability for memory-heavy operations that do not require high CPU throughput. Tradeoffs include modest processing performance and complete reliance on attached persistent disks for storage. Recommended use cases include in-memory caching, light database instances, low-concurrency web services, and background data processing tasks where memory footprint is the principal bottleneck.
